results.summary: This project implements a tiny binarized neural network with eight output neurons in Verilog. Inputs are shared between parameter loading and data input depending on the setup pin, and the eight outputs are either neuron results or a parameter value. The documentation consists only of pin names and a TODO for both the operation and test sections, so the internal architecture and weight-loading scheme cannot be determined. The design is incomplete and lacks sufficient documentation to describe its full functionality.

This project implements a simple cellular automaton on a 7-segment display using about 200 logic gates, where each segment lives or dies based on the number of living neighbours it touches. It is tested on the standard Tiny Tapeout board using DIP switches for load, run mode and clock division, with no external hardware required. The documentation includes detailed operating instructions and a set of puzzles about the automaton's behaviour, making it a notable educational design. The design is a puzzle game that demonstrates cellular automaton principles.

This project implements a shift register that loads a 6-bit input and shifts it out while encoding the bits for display. The write_not_shift control selects between loading and shifting, and the encoded bits are shown one at a time on an 8-segment display with the decimal point indicating the clock. It is tested using the standard Tiny Tapeout board with DIP switches for input and a display for output. The design is a simple demonstration of shift register and encoding logic.

This project is a basic arithmetic building block that performs addition and logic operations. It is implemented in Wokwi and requires no external hardware beyond the standard board switches and LEDs. The design is combinational and can be used as a simple ALU. It is suitable for educational purposes.

This project is a finite state machine that controls LED outputs based on input conditions. It is implemented in Wokwi and uses standard board switches and LEDs for testing. The design is intended for industrial control applications. It demonstrates sequential logic and state-based control.

This project is an experiment to characterise the temperature-versus-frequency relationship of a ring oscillator. It requires UART connectivity to read the frequency measurements. The design includes a temperature sensor interface and an oscillator circuit. It is intended for process characterization and sensor interfacing.

This project uses a 4-bit counter to sequence and drive a 7-segment display. It is implemented in Wokwi and uses standard board switches and LEDs for testing. The design is a simple counter with display output. It demonstrates basic counting and display driving.

This project implements a BCD counter that drives a 7-segment display. It is implemented in Wokwi and uses standard board switches and LEDs for testing. The design includes a clock generator and counter logic. It demonstrates binary-coded decimal counting.

This project implements an error-correction encoder that loads a 6-bit input and shifts it out while encoding the bits for transmission. The write_not_shift control selects between loading and shifting, and the encoded bits are shown one at a time on an 8-segment display. It is tested using the standard Tiny Tapeout board with DIP switches and a display. The design demonstrates error-correction encoding and shift register operation.

This project implements a neural network encoder that loads a 6-bit input and shifts it out while encoding the bits for display. The write_not_shift control selects between loading and shifting, and the encoded bits are shown one at a time on an 8-segment display. It is tested using the standard Tiny Tapeout board with DIP switches and a display. The design demonstrates neural network encoding and shift register operation.
